title: Why Do Team Members Work So Hard
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that leaders chasing motivation through praise, compensation, and status are missing a deeper driver: most people work hard primarily for the people they love, not for workplace rewards. The best leaders, the author says, ask not just what motivates team members but for whom, and then build practices around that insight, from inviting family photos and milestones into the workplace to designing family-inclusive events and flexible policies. Leading by example matters too, with leaders openly prioritizing their own families as a model for the team. The piece closes with a quote elevating family from 'important' to 'everything' as the real engine behind workplace effort and sacrifice.
points: Standard motivators like praise, status, and compensation don't fully explain why people work hard
The deeper driver is sacrifice for loved ones, especially children, partners, and family
Leaders who grasp this build family-inclusive practices, from photos at desks to flexible policies
Leading by example, prioritizing one's own family visibly, reinforces the message for the team
quotes: The success of any organization depends on team members working hard and making the necessary sacrifices to get the job done.
They not only ask what team members work so hard for — but also for whom.
They work hard for the people they love. First and foremost, team members work hard and sacrifice for their children, their partners, and their families.
Leaders who understand this universal motivation operate differently than others.
Most of all, they lead by example, showcasing their own families and loved ones and making them a priority in everything they do at work.
